messages:
maria: Quick sync — follow-up from the panel auth RFC: implications for query-layer caching and dashboard latency. TL;DR: the auth-surface split (edge vs service) could cause cache fragmentation and extra cold SLOs.
ben: Do you have concrete perf numbers or is this based on estimates?
maria: Local harness results: inline auth adds ~1.8ms median for a single lookup. But if we change cache_key to include tenant scoping (per-tenant keys) miss rate rises ~25% on our multi-tenant test, blowing token-level cache efficiency.
eva: Could we use short-lived signed tokens so cache sees same key across tenants? Token contains tenant-hash + exp 5m. That keeps cache stable for reads.
charlie: Signed tokens shift trust/troubles to clients — revocation is harder and control-plane invalidation becomes messy. For Hosted we need immediate revocation in some cases.
maria: True. Another pattern: auth sidecar that canonicalizes cache_key to panel:{panel_id}:view and populates a shared cache with tenant masks. Sidecar adds a hop but lets cache stay shared.
sanjay: Sidecar hop increases p99 by ~7ms in my harness when multiplexed. We should compare that to the 25% miss-cost (which manifests as extra backend queries). Which is cheaper in the p99 budget? @leigh any SLO margin numbers?
leigh: Console dashboard p99 target is 200ms; current headroom ~40ms on average. An extra 7ms seems fine in isolation, but multiplexed pipelines + auth sidecars could amplify. Need end-to-end run.
ben: What about a hybrid: signed tokens for read-only panels (fast cacheable path) + sidecar for write/privileged routes where revocation matters. That reduces revocation surface while retaining cache efficiency for common paths.
maria: Hybrid seems pragmatic. We should decide config surface: route-level flag or attribute-driven policy? Draft config snippet below as a sketch:
```
console.routes:
  - path: /panel/read
    auth_mode: signed_token
    cache_key: panel:{panel_id}:view
  - path: /panel/write
    auth_mode: sidecar
    cache_key: panel:{panel_id}:tenant:{tenant_id}
```
charlie: Also need end-to-end auth audit traces — correlation-id that ties tokens/sidecar decisions back to control-plane actions so we can invalidate or trace leaks.
eva: Ops note: constrain token audience and scope aggressively; for embedded dashboards limit lifetime to 1-3m and require audience checks. Also add KMS rotation guidance in the operator playbook.
maria: Agreed. Action items: (1) prototype hybrid in staging, (2) run perf tests with realistic multiplexing and cache-population, (3) update config docs and operator guide with token rotation and revocation caveats. I'll open an RFC follow-up PR with benchmarks.
sanjay: Add telemetry bullet: per-route cache hitrate, broken down by auth_mode and tenant churn. That will show real-world hit fragmentation.
maria: Good call — I'll include telemetry + dashboards in the PR. Thanks all :tada:
